Your check did find a real fault, though. From Tuesday to Thursday, before the week's FantasyPros ranks come out, every rest-of-season rate was dropping its FantasyPros half. In the 2021-25 backtest, keeping last week's rank does better: error 2.22-2.34 vs 2.37-2.55. That's fixed now, with a test (projections/current.py; docs/projections.md). Walker goes from 21.6 to 19.7 ppg, Washington from 12.25 to 12.06, and Deebo is unchanged.

A 6,000-sim recheck gives +$2, and if Washington is really 2 ppg better than projected it's -$8. So the target is about break-even. Only the opening (two 2027 2nds instead of the 2029 1st: you +$13 to +$18, Ben +$5) is clearly in your favor, and I wouldn't go up to the 2029 1st. Re-ran it: trades.State.evaluate at 6,000 sims for every WR/RB/TE under 2027 contract on the six sellers (Matt, Qasim, Max, Ryan, Ben, Mike; decide_deadline). Rosters and cap come from the site snapshot of 2026-11-19 13:00 UTC, and projections from proj_ros at 12:45 UTC.

Short answer: picks alone don't buy much. Only one seller player is a big upgrade over Washington (WR3, 12.1 ppg) or Irving (flex, 14.3), and he can't be bought with picks.

- Kenneth Walker III (Ben, $67 now, $70 in 2027): +32 lineup points rest of season; 1st 57%->65%, title 40%->46%. Your in-season cap room is -$15, so with a player over $20 the 25% salary rule needs salary coming back. Picks only is illegal. The legal version is the card's: Dart + Washington + Fannin + picks. That's you +$6 with the 2029 1st, or +$17 with two 2027 2nds instead.
- George Pickens (Ryan, $71/$75): +12 points, but you -$13 even for nothing, because his 2027-28 salary is worth -41 points over three years. Picks only is illegal too. Pass.
- Cheap 2027 contracts, legal for picks: Chris Olave (Max, $15/$30): +5 points, you +$4 for nothing, Max +$18. Michael Wilson (Matt, $1/$2): +5, you +$4, Matt -$2 (a 2029 3rd closes it). Malik Nabers (Qasim, $7/$8): +5, you +$2 for a 2029 3rd, Qasim +$7. Luther Burden III: +1 point, break-even. Each moves your 1st-place odds 1-3 points. Title odds move by less than the sim's noise.

So Walker is the only target worth a 1st, and only in the card's form. The others are worth $2-4 to you. Pay no more than a 3rd: a 2nd is $21-23 of later value and a 1st is $57-65.

The 2027 cap: added salary doesn't change your auction, since you're over after the Gibbs match either way ($0 adds only). The binding limit is the Lamb tag, which must fit under the $300 cap (league.yaml). Your outlook has $350 committed for 2027 including Lamb $96 and Gibbs $135, so $119 before the tag. That leaves about $85 of net added 2027 salary before the tag stops fitting. Net added salary: Walker as carded +$9, Olave +$30, Nabers +$8, Wilson +$2. All fit. Walker for picks only (+$70) plus anything else would not.

What would change this: a seller's WR getting a bigger role (Olave 12.7 and Nabers 12.6 ppg project only just above Washington's 12.1), an injury to Lamb, Chase or Gibbs (which raises every target's gain), or Russ, Johnny or Zach dropping into selling. I agree with the reframe, and it changes the shopping list. The goal is now 2027 lineup points from cheap contracts, bought with picks, with no 2026 player going out. Picks-only deals for players under $20 meet that: no salary matching is needed and your lineup this year doesn't change. These are reads from the data, not model runs. Player data is from the 2026-11-19 21:42 UTC snapshot.

**What you have for 2027 under contract (with Lamb tagged and Gibbs matched)**
- QB: Mahomes 275 projected points
- RB: Gibbs 232, Irving 194
- WR: Lamb 206, Washington 161, Robinson 115
- TE: Fannin 135
- Flex: Kittle 124 (TEs can play flex)

Chase and Hubbard leave, so your holes are WR3 (115) and flex (124). After the auction, the leftovers on seller rosters project about 85–100 points (Douglas 86, Freiermuth 90, Tucker 103). Anything above roughly 125 is a real gain. Each player helps less than the last, because the second one replaces Kittle, not Robinson.

**Best fits: big 2027 points, cheap in picks because their value is mostly 2027**
1. **Chris Olave (Max): $30 in 2027, 174 points, 3-year surplus only 16.** About 59 points over Robinson, worth about $31 at the league's $0.53 a point. A 2nd is worth about $23 and a 3rd about $23 by your pick values. The earlier answer said Max comes out ahead even giving him away for nothing. Offer a 3rd and go no higher than one of your 2027 2nds. The downside is $45 in 2028.
2. **Jaylen Warren (Max): $12, 162 points, surplus 28.** Takes the flex from Kittle for about 38 more points. Pair him with Olave in one Max deal.
3. **Rome Odunze (Ryan): $8, 146 points, surplus 15.** A smaller gain of 22–31 points, but he should cost a 3rd or less.

**Better players who cost much more:** Nabers (186 points, surplus 70), Burden (159, 101), Concepcion (151, 142), Boston (149, 129). Rookie-deal RBs like Jeanty, Hampton, Judkins and Jeremiyah Love have surplus of 169–236, more than a 1st (worth 138). You'd be paying for 2028–29 value. That's not crazy, since you project 5th in 2028 and 9th in 2029, but it's a different goal from this one.

**A lever we haven't used: your second RFA slot**
You get two RFAs a team, and Gibbs uses one. RFA matches are allowed to put you over the cap, and in 2027 extra salary costs you nothing, because you're limited to $0 adds either way. So you could trade for an expiring cheap player now and use that slot to keep him on a one-year deal at whatever the market bid is. Two examples:
- Chase Brown (Max): $4 now, 183 points; Max's own projected RFA price is about $66
- Rashee Rice (Matt): $6 now, 163 points; about $38

That could beat any player under contract. The catch is that the RFA price is set by other owners' bids, and I can't simulate that.

**Cap check**
The limit is the Lamb tag, which has to fit under $300 when tags happen in June–July. RFA matches come later, in August.
- Your outlook says $350 committed. That implies about $85 of room for added 2027 salary.
- Your listed 2027 contracts add up to $311, which would mean about $124 of room. I can't account for the $39 difference, so plan on $85.
- Olave and Warren add $42 together and fit.

**Two things to settle before any offer**
- Run it in the models: Olave + Warren from Max for a 2027 2nd or 3rd, and the RFA route on Brown or Rice, including the likely match price and whether a designated player's starting bid counts against the tag deadline.
- The trade deadline is the end of Week 14. You have room to drop bench players like Gesicki, Deebo or Gainwell to make roster space.
